🚁 CHATSWORTH FROM ABOVE | EPISODE 11 — CROSSMOOR

We've reached another major milestone in our journey through Chatsworth!

From Unit 1, Havenside, all the way to UNIT 11 — CROSSMOOR, we've explored the numbered neighbourhoods of Chatsworth through drone cinematography, historical research and local storytelling.

And today, we've arrived at the final numbered unit in the original Chatsworth sequence!

Welcome to CROSSMOOR!

Situated in the greater Chatsworth area of Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, Crossmoor is a community with its own history, schools, sporting achievements, businesses and familiar landmarks.

But where does the name Crossmoor come from? How did Unit 11 develop? And what makes this part of Chatsworth different from the neighbourhoods we've already explored?

Join me as we take to the skies and discover Crossmoor from an entirely different perspective.

📍 PLACES AND LANDMARKS FEATURED

🏫 CROSSMOOR SECONDARY SCHOOL

Established on 16 January 1978, the school originally opened as Chatsworth No. 63, with an enrolment of 920 learners and Mr G. P. Desai as its first principal.

We explore the school's history and some of its educational achievements.

🏫 PRIMARY SCHOOLS OF CROSSMOOR

• Crossmead Primary School
• M. Padavatan Primary School
• Brooklyn Heights Primary School

🛒 CROSSMOOR SHOPPING CENTRE

A familiar local shopping destination serving residents and businesses in the surrounding area.

🏏 SPORTING HISTORY

Discover Crossmoor's connections to the sporting history of Chatsworth, including local cricket development, football and the contribution of sporting organisations such as Chatsworth Sporting and Moorcross Sporting Club.

🏘️ BOTTLEBRUSH AND SURROUNDING COMMUNITIES

We explore the geographical relationship between Crossmoor and neighbouring Bottlebrush, including how different residential communities developed across the surrounding landscape.

📍 CROSSMOOR DRIVE AND RESIDENTIAL AREAS

From Crossmoor Drive and Golden Poppy Crescent to the surrounding residential streets, hills and valleys, experience Unit 11 through original aerial footage.

────────────────────

📖 THE HISTORY OF CROSSMOOR

Crossmoor became known as Unit 11 as Chatsworth's numbered residential areas developed.

Its name is commonly linked to the idea of crossing open, uncultivated land, reflecting the area's historical landscape.

In this episode, we explore its development, educational institutions, local sporting history and the relationship between Crossmoor and neighbouring communities.

Crossmoor marks the final numbered stop in our journey — but the story of Greater Chatsworth doesn't end here!

There are still surrounding communities with fascinating histories waiting to be explored.

entries.title: Thompsons Bay, Ballito | Charlie’s Pool & the Hole in the Wall
entries.description:
Discover Thompsons Bay, one of the best-known coastal landmarks on KwaZulu-Natal’s Dolphin Coast. Just north of Ballito, this beautiful stretch of coastline brings together sandy beaches, rugged rock formations, the Indian Ocean and the famous tidal pool known as Charlie’s Pool.

Built in 1962 by Charles de Charmoy, his family and farm labourers, the pool took around seven weeks and approximately 2,000 pockets of cement to complete. It measures about 106 metres long and 30 metres wide. More than six decades later, it remains a popular place for swimming, relaxing and snorkelling among the fish and marine life.

The Hole in the Wall is a natural rock arch beside the pool. Beyond it is a smaller beach and rocky pools where shells and marine life can be found. Access can be affected by the tide, so check local conditions before exploring the passage. 

Overlooking the bay are the white, Greek-inspired buildings of Santorini Estate, in Shaka’s Rock. The estate has access to Thompsons Bay and the neighbouring semi-private Perissa beach.

📍 Thompsons Bay, Ballito, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa

CHATSWORTH FROM ABOVE | EPISODE 9 — MOORTON & RISECLIFF

Our journey through Chatsworth continues, and this time we're exploring UNIT 9 — MOORTON & RISECLIFF!

After visiting Silverglen, our unofficial Unit 8, we're returning to Chatsworth's numbered residential units to discover the history, landmarks and communities that make this part of Durban unique.

But there's something interesting about Unit 9.

Although Moorton and Risecliff are closely connected, they're actually recognised as separate residential localities. And some roads commonly associated with Montford, including sections of Road 701, are also identified as Risecliff addresses.

So where does Risecliff fit into the wider Chatsworth landscape?

Join me as we take to the skies and explore the history, schools, important landmarks and changing residential landscape of Moorton and Risecliff.

We also explore the development of Moorton during the apartheid era, the origins of its name and an interesting historical reference that identifies Risecliff as Unit 8 — even though other accounts describe Unit 8 as missing from Chatsworth's numbered sequence.

entries.title: Muscle Cracker Fight ! | Fishing Bluff for the First time
entries.description:
Muscle Cracker Caught! 🎣🔥

For the first time, I headed out to **Bluff, Durban** to try my luck at a new fishing spot — and it turned into an awesome session!

I was hoping to find some good fish, and eventually the rod loaded up with a **Muscle Cracker**! This was my first time fishing Bluff, so it was great to explore a new area and see what the fishing had to offer.

Join me for another South African fishing adventure as I explore the coastline, chase some fish and enjoy a day out on the water.

If you enjoy **fishing, surf fishing, South African fishing, catch-and-cook videos, outdoor adventures and exploring new fishing spots**, make sure to LIKE, COMMENT and SUBSCRIBE to **KayzAdventures** for more! 🎣🌊
